newsitem.title: UK: UK to decide shortly on European FLA aircraft.
newsitem.headline: UK to decide shortly on European FLA aircraft.

text.p: Britain's Ministry of Defence (MOD) said on Tuesday it will decide soon on whether to rejoin Europe's Future Large Aircraft (FLA) military transporter project and on how many of the aircraft it wants.
"We will be reaching conclusions on this as soon as we can," a ministry spokesman said. "No final decisions have been made but we do expect to take a decision shortly," he added.
For the last two years Britain has said it could order up to 40 or 50 of the turboprop aircraft to replace the rest of its ageing fleet of Lockeed Hercules C-130s from year 2004.
But there are fears that the Royal Air Force wants to drop the embryonic FLA project altogether or at least minimise its order in favour of buying more Lockheed C130Js.
Industry sources said the RAF has also been considering an offer by McDonnell Douglas to lease to Britain its giant new jet-powered C-17 Globemaster strategic transporter.
A report in industry magazine Flight International this week said that the Royal Air Force (RAF) has concluded that it would only need 25 FLAs, compared with the 40-50 aircraft originally envisaged.
In comparison according to industry sources the smaller tactical FLA transporter is likely to carry a price tag of around $70 million compared to around $200 million for the C-17.

British Aerospace, the British member of the eight-nation industrial consortium seeking to build the FLA, confirmed that the number of aircraft ordered by Britain would be critical in determining its workshare on the programme.
"The workshare is dependent on the number of aircraft required by an individual country," a spokesman said.
"Our understanding is that there is still a (British) requirement as stated for between 40 and 50 aircraft and we have not been informed of any change in that position," he added.

The FLA consortium, which would operate as an expanded military branch of the four-nation civil aircraft manufacturer Airbus Industrie, expects member governments to make an initial "request for proposals" sometime this year, the BAe spokesman said.
